claim: For each pair of integers \(2\le m<n\), let \(G=P_m\square P_n\) be the unlabelled simple grid and let \(u=(1,0)\), \(v=(0,1)\). Under ordinary colour refinement from one uniform vertex colour, \(c_r(u)=c_r(v)\) for every \(0\le r\le m-2\), but \(c_{m-1}(u)\ne c_{m-1}(v)\). In fact, for adjacency matrix \(A\) and \(b(w)=4-\deg(w)\), the difference \((A^k b)(u)-(A^k b)(v)\) is zero when \(0\le k<m-2\) and one when \(k=m-2\). Thus \(\rho(G)\ge m-1\), and the least quantifier rank of a distinguishing unary two-variable counting-logic formula on these pointed vertices is exactly \(m-1\).
integrity: Infinite proof via quadrant walk-tree interchange and a unique first defect-walk contribution; computational verification is supplementary.
scientific_limitations: Only one natural pair of vertices in each non-square grid is considered; no exact global stabilization formula, coordinate labels, or colored initial conditions are claimed. Search coverage cannot establish universal novelty.
title: Exact axis-orientation delay in rectangular grid color refinement
